# The from-zero job's known doctor failures (#2013 X1): findings on a fresh
# runner that the epic already owns. One entry per line, "<darwin|linux> <text>",
# where <text> is a fixed substring of the [FAIL] line. Each entry is preceded by
# a comment naming its owner and by an "# example:" line quoting the [FAIL] line
# it was written for; tests/from-zero-doctor-gate.bats asserts the text is in its
# example. The gate fails on a [FAIL] no entry matches AND on an entry no [FAIL]
# matches, so an entry leaves when its owner's fix lands: the list only shrinks.
# A new defect never goes here without an owner on the #2013 ledger.

# owner: PLAT-001c tasks.md, kubectl as a `# mise: cli` pin (waits on the release whose version probe reads it)
# example: [FAIL] kubectl not in PATH
darwin kubectl not in PATH

# owner: #2384 CLI-105 (agy's MCP master config is written only by the setup
# twins; agy reaches the macOS runner through mise since #2013 P5c)
# example: [FAIL] master mcp_config.json missing at /Users/runner/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json (run setup)
darwin master mcp_config.json missing

# owner: #2013 S2 (hive supervision: launchd on macOS, `hive service install` on Linux)
# A runner has no daemon, so hive's verdict is "down", or "unverified listener"
# when another program holds the derived port (run 38372164624; hive#492). One
# entry covers both: two would leave one stale on every run.
# example: [FAIL] the hive daemon is down, so the hive MCP server fails in every agent (`hive client` never starts a server of its own). macOS has no hive supervisor yet: start `hive serve` by hand, then confirm with `hive service status`.
darwin the hive daemon is

linux the hive daemon is
